trips.name: Moss Park
trips.card_teaser: A great county campground with shade and sun, fun amenities, and stunning views of Kennedy Space Center. What better time to decorate a campsite than the holidays?
trips.intro: A great county campground with shade and sun, fun amenities, and stunning views of Kennedy Space Center. What better time to decorate a campsite than the holidays?
body_paragraphs: Many people have expressed a joy in camping over the holidays — when else can you decorate your campsite? But the season can make it hard to get away. Moss Park solves that: a great escape that's still close to home.

Moss Park sits between Lake Mary Jane and Lake Hart, about 20 minutes from Orlando International Airport. Expect shaded, spacious sites, a swimming beach, boat ramps for fishing and paddling, hiking trails, and regular visits from deer and sandhill cranes.

As always, you'll need to book your own site directly through the park. Once you've got your reservation, let us know which site you picked so we can add you to the group camping map — that's how the rest of the group finds you once you're there.
facts: Swim beach, boat ramp, trails, pavilions
trips.note: Reservations go through Orange County Parks & Recreation, not through our group. Book your own site, then share your site number with the group.

trips.name: Wickham Park
trips.card_teaser: A large campground with lots going on — an arts & crafts fair, hiking trails, disc golf, and only 15 minutes from the beach. The hardest part is deciding what to do first.
trips.intro: A large campground with lots going on — an arts & crafts fair, hiking trails, disc golf, and only 15 minutes from the beach. The hardest part is deciding what to do first.
body_paragraphs: Sometimes you want the beach, other times you want a festival — why not both? Wickham Park puts you close to Melbourne's beaches while the park itself keeps you busy with its own art and crafts fair, hiking trails, and disc golf course.
This 391-acre Brevard County park offers full-hookup campsites, fishing lakes, an archery range, and a dog park, all on flat, easy terrain that's simple to navigate with the whole family.
You'll book your own site directly with Brevard County, then let us know which site you picked so we can add you to the group camping map.
facts: Disc golf, archery, fishing lakes, dog park

trips.name: Jetty Park
trips.card_teaser: Beach Baptism weekend, now a full weekend at the beach with cruise ship views. Air-conditioned cabins are still available — but this one books out fast.
trips.intro: Beach Baptism weekend doesn't have to just be a day. Enjoy a full weekend at the beach with views of the cruise ships. There are even still cabins available, complete with beds and AC!
body_paragraphs: Jetty Park is a wildly popular campground right on the beach in Port Canaveral — a perfect place to enjoy the sand, fish off the pier, surf some waves, and watch the cruise ships head out.
This is our biggest group trip of the year, timed around Beach Baptism weekend. Jetty Park does book out far in advance, so if you want to join us, don't wait too long to reserve your spot.

If you're tent camping, stick to a dome tent — it's highly recommended. The wind off the water gets serious out there, and a few of our group members have lost rigid, square-frame tents that couldn't flex with the gusts.

Heads up on checkout timing: Beach Baptism itself happens at Lori Wilson Park down the road, and campers/RVs are not allowed there. If you check out of Jetty Park on Sunday morning, you won't have anywhere to leave your camper during the baptism — so plan on a later checkout, or line up somewhere else to park it first.
Book through the link below, then let us know which site or cabin you picked so we can add you to the group camping map.
facts: Plenty of standard sites & A/C cabins
Dome tents only — high winds have taken down rigid frames
Avoid Sunday — no camper parking at Lori Wilson Park

trips.name: Lake Louisa State Park
trips.special_event: Sites Fully Booked — Day Visitors Welcome
trips.card_teaser: Trade the ocean for spring-fed lakes at this sprawling state park in the Clermont hills. Camping sites are fully booked for this one, but the park itself is open to visit for the day.
trips.intro: Trade the ocean for spring-fed lakes at this sprawling state park in the Clermont hills. Camping sites are fully booked for this one, but the park itself is open to visit for the day.
body_paragraphs: Lake Louisa State Park trades salt water for spring-fed lakes — three of them, tucked into the rolling citrus-country hills of Clermont. It's a different kind of camping weekend: quieter water, longer trails, and a campground built for settling in rather than rushing around.

The park sits about 45 minutes southwest of Orlando, between Lake Louisa, Lake Hammond, and Lake Dixie. Expect 60 full-facility sites with 30- and 50-amp hookups, plus cabins and a few glamping-style bell tents if you'd rather skip the tent setup. Bring a kayak or paddleboard — the lakes are made for it — or walk the seven miles of paved road and twenty miles of trail.

Camping sites for this trip are completely booked — there's nothing left to reserve for the group. The park is still open to the public for the day, though: come out and join us for a few hours of kayaking, swimming, or trail time, even if you're not staying overnight.
facts: 3 lakes, kayaking, cabins & glamping, 20 mi of trails
trips.note: Camping sites are fully booked for this trip. The park remains open to day visitors for $5 per vehicle, 8am to sunset — no reservation needed to stop by for the day.

trips.name: Florida RV SuperShow
trips.card_teaser: North America's largest RV show rolls into Tampa for its 41st year. We won't all be camping together for this one, but however you're attending, join us Saturday night for dinner.
trips.intro: North America's largest RV show rolls into Tampa for its 41st year — 1.5 million square feet of new models, parts, and accessories. We won't all be camping together for this one, but however you're attending, join us Saturday night for dinner.
body_paragraphs: The Florida RV SuperShow is the premier RV event in the region, running January 15–17, 2027 at the Florida State Fairgrounds in Tampa. As North America's largest RV show, it spans 1.5 million square feet with hundreds of new models, parts, and accessories on display.

This one's a little different — a lot of our members have talked about going, so we're turning it into a group weekend even though we won't all be camping together. Because the show is so big, campgrounds nearby fill up fast (many are already sold out), so whether you camp, book a hotel, or just make it a day trip is entirely up to you.

However you're attending, join us Saturday, January 16th at 6:30pm for dinner at Portillo's in Brandon — a quick-service spot known for hot dogs, Italian beef, cheese fries, and milkshakes, with plenty of room for a crowd.
Sign up below so we know how many to expect at dinner.
facts: Book early — sites nearby fill up fast
1.5M sq ft · North America's largest RV show
trips.note: This one isn't a shared group campsite — camp, book a hotel, or make it a day trip, whatever works for you. Sign up so we know how many to expect at Portillo's Saturday night.

trips.card_teaser: A large campground with lots going on — right in the middle of our stay, the park hosts the Space Coast Holiday Food Fest & Craft Fair. Add hiking trails, disc golf, and a beach only 15 minutes away, and the hardest part is deciding what to do first.
trips.intro: A large campground with lots going on — right in the middle of our stay, the park hosts the Space Coast Holiday Food Fest & Craft Fair. Add hiking trails, disc golf, and a beach only 15 minutes away, and the hardest part is deciding what to do first.

This 391-acre Brevard County park offers full-hookup campsites, fishing lakes, an archery range, and a dog park, all on flat, easy terrain that's simple to navigate with the whole family.

This trip lines up with the 3rd Annual Space Coast Holiday Food Fest & Craft Fair, happening right there in the park on Saturday, December 5th from 12–9pm. Expect a craft fair marketplace, a $1–$5 a la carte tasting menu, a kid zone with bounce houses and train rides, axe throwing, holiday movie projections, and visits from Santa and the Grinch — with proceeds benefiting The Children's Hunger Project. It's a separate ticket from your campsite, so grab one below if you want in.

trips.name: Moss Park
trips.card_teaser: Tentative for now — a 3-day weekend at our local campground, just 15 minutes from church. We're hoping to snag Moss Park's large group site so all 6 of our camps/tents can stay together in one spot.
trips.intro: Tentative for now — a 3-day weekend at our local campground, just 15 minutes from church. We're hoping to snag Moss Park's large group site so all 6 of our camps/tents can stay together in one spot.
body_paragraphs: Moss Park is our local campground — just 15 minutes from church, sitting between Lake Mary Jane and Lake Hart about 20 minutes from Orlando International Airport. Expect shaded, spacious grounds, a swimming beach, boat ramps for fishing and paddling, hiking trails, and regular visits from deer and sandhill cranes.

Being so close to home makes this a great, low-pressure pick for anyone new to camping — no long drive, no big commitment, just an easy trial run for the group. It lands over a 3-day weekend, so there's time to actually settle in rather than just passing through.

This trip would also be a little different from our usual setup: instead of everyone booking separate sites, Moss Park lets us reserve one large group site big enough for 6 camps/tents together — so the whole crew stays side by side instead of spread across the campground.

The catch is timing. Orange County Parks & Recreation only opens reservations 40 days before arrival, so we can't actually lock in the group site until closer to early January 2027. Consider this a save-the-date for now — more details (and a firm booking) will be posted here as soon as the reservation window opens.
